title: Oct 3 Results + Oct 4 Preview: Three Out of Four Ain't Bad
summary: 75% accuracy on Oct 3 with three wins. Milwaukee stays hot for tomorrow's top pick.

content.value:
## A Solid Friday Night

Look, I've been doing this long enough to know that 3-1 nights are what keep you in the game. We hit 75% on Friday's slate, and the only stumble was Cleveland—where we learned once again that October baseball has a way of humbling even the most confident models. The Guardians at home seemed like a safe play at 52%, but the Sox had other ideas. Tale as old as time.

## What Worked (And What Didn't)

The Dodgers pick at 65% was the crown jewel—LA at home against Atlanta played out exactly as expected. The pitching matchup favored them, and they delivered. Tampa Bay squeaking past the Yankees was another win, though 59% confidence meant we weren't exactly shocked by the tight scoreline.

Milwaukee covering against San Diego gave us our third hit, and here's where it gets interesting: we're going right back to that well tomorrow. Sometimes you ride the hot hand, and sometimes the hot hand is a team that just keeps finding ways to win at home.

The Cleveland miss? Chalk it up to variance. At 52%, we were basically calling a coin flip, and the coin landed on the other side. No shame in that.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Back to Milwaukee

I've seen this movie before. When a team wins at home and you get them again the next day with decent pitching, you don't overthink it. The Brewers are our top pick for October 4th, even though the model is giving us a cautious 50% confidence.

Michael King takes the hill for San Diego—solid arm, no question. But Logan Henderson at home in Milwaukee has shown he can navigate pressure situations. The Brewers' bullpen is rested, the crowd will be loud, and momentum is a real thing in October, no matter what the analytics say.

content.value:
## The Bottom Line

A 75% night keeps you ahead of the curve. Three wins, one loss, and a chance to run it back with Milwaukee tomorrow. I've been around long enough to know you take these nights, bank the wins, and keep grinding.

The Brewers at even odds? I'll take that action every time. See you tomorrow when we find out if experience trumps caution once again.
